advances: Conditional normal-localized inequality with possible mass deficit on the zero set. The full test cone, pointwise remainder and selector convergence remain hypotheses of an application. The result allows a nonzero defect and yields no numerical depth bound.

proof:
Truncated positive logarithms extend continuously through zero, so weak convergence and monotone convergence give $\int\ell_+\,d\eta\le\sup_j\int\ell_{j,+}\,d\eta_j$. On compact subsets of $\{L>0\}$ the logarithms converge uniformly. Testing with continuous functions supported there identifies both ordinary parts, using $\eta_j\rightharpoonup\eta$ and $W_j\eta_j\rightharpoonup W\eta$. The limiting measures are positive and ordered, and since $\eta(Z)=0$, their restrictions to $Z$ are precisely $0\le a\le b$.

A finite convex function defined on an open convex neighborhood of the current compact body range can be used as a test on that range. Choose a compact neighborhood of the range in that open set. The affine supports at points of this compact neighborhood have uniformly bounded slopes by local Lipschitz continuity and compactness. Their supremum is globally finite and agrees on the range. In particular $\Phi=(\ell_j-1)_+$ is allowed, by positivity of $L_j$ in a convex neighborhood. Set $\psi=1$ in this test. Because $W_j\ge0$ and $\sup_j|\beta_j|<\infty$, the inequality gives
$$
\lambda_j\int\ell_j(\ell_j-1)_+\,d\eta_j
\le (|\beta_j|+C\lambda_j)\int\ell_{j,+}\,d\eta_j.
$$
For $s\ge0$ one has $s^2\le s(s-1)_++s$. This proves boundedness of the quadratic measures. They converge to zero against continuous functions supported where $L>0$, so any limit $q$ is carried by $Z$.

First assume $f$ is strictly positive on the current ranges and their neighborhoods and bounded below away from zero on $X$, for instance by replacing a nonnegative $f$ by $f+\delta$. The function
$$
F_T(a,b)=\max\{0,a\log(a/b)-Ta\},\qquad a,b>0,
$$
is convex as a maximum of zero and a relative-entropy perspective minus a linear term. It is nondecreasing in $a$ because the derivative of the positive branch in $a$ is $\log(a/b)-T+1>1$, and nonincreasing in $b$. Applying convexity of $f$, concavity of $L_j$, these monotonicities, and joint convexity in turn shows that $F_T(f(w),L_j(w))$ is convex on the positive neighborhood. Its finite extension above is an allowed test for this same $j$.

Fix $T>\sup_X\log f$ and let $c=T-\log f>0$ on $X$. The test on the boundary is
$$
f(\ell_j-c)_+=f\ell_{j,+}-f\min\{\ell_{j,+},c\}.
$$
The minimum on the right is bounded and continuous as a function of $(L_j,w)$ on the support, extending across $L_j=0$ by $c(w)$ (use $c$ also for negative inputs). Uniform convergence of $L_j$ and weak convergence of the two selector measures therefore give
$$
\lim_j\int\psi(W_j-\beta_j) f(\ell_j-c)_+\,d\eta_j
=\int\psi(W-\beta)f(\ell-c)_+\,d\eta+\int\psi f\,d(a-\beta b).
$$
On the positive branch $\ell_j>c>0$, and everywhere
$$
|\lambda_j\ell_j f(\ell_j-c)_+-\lambda_j f\ell_{j,+}^2|
\le\lambda_j f c\,\ell_{j,+}.
$$
Its integral tends to zero for fixed $T$, so the logarithmic term tends to $\int\psi f\,dq$. The remainder is bounded in absolute value by $C\lambda_j\|\psi f\|_\infty\int\ell_{j,+}d\eta_j$, which tends to zero. Pass to the limit in the test inequality and then send $T\to\infty$, using the integrable domination by $\ell_+$ for the ordinary part. Finally send $\delta\downarrow0$ when using $f+\delta$. The result follows.

statement:
Let $U$ and $X$ be compact, with $U$ a metric space of recorded normals and $X$ in a finite-dimensional affine physical space. Let finite positive measures $\eta_j$ on $U\times X$ converge weakly to $\eta$. For each $j$ the physical projection of $\operatorname{supp}\eta_j$ lies in a compact convex body range on which the finite minimum of affine functions $L_j$ is positive. Assume the $L_j$ converge uniformly on $X$ to a nonnegative $L$, $\eta(Z)=0$ for $Z=\{(u,w):L(w)=0\}$, and $\sup_j\int \ell_{j,+}\,d\eta_j<\infty$, where $\ell_j=-\log L_j$ on the support of $\eta_j$. Suppose $0\le W_j\le1$, $W_j\eta_j\rightharpoonup W\eta$, $\beta_j\to\beta$, and $\lambda_j>0$ tends to zero. Assume $|R_j|\le C\lambda_j$ $\eta_j$-almost everywhere and that the common inequality
$$
\int \psi(u)\Phi(w)(W_j-\beta_j+\lambda_j\ell_j+R_j)\,d\eta_j\le0
$$
holds for every continuous $\psi\ge0$ and every globally finite convex $\Phi$ on the physical space.

The measures $\lambda_j\ell_{j,+}^2\eta_j$ have bounded masses. Along any joint weakly converging subsequence write the limits of $\ell_{j,+}\eta_j$, $W_j\ell_{j,+}\eta_j$, and $\lambda_j\ell_{j,+}^2\eta_j$ as $\ell_+\eta+b$, $W\ell_+\eta+a$, and $q$, respectively, with $\ell=-\log L$ off $Z$. Then $0\le a\le b$ and $q\ge0$, all three supported on $Z$. For every such $\psi$ and every nonnegative globally finite convex $f$,
$$
\int\psi(u)f(w)\,d(a+q)\le\beta\int\psi(u)f(w)\,db .
$$
In particular $a(U\times X)+q(U\times X)\le\beta b(U\times X)$.
